extracted.intended_audience: linguists, humor researchers, and comedy writers interested in punchline structure
extracted.subtask_description: Analytic criteria for evaluating or constructing joke punchlines, focusing on terminal tension, internal pulse architecture, and the logical devices that produce surprise. Useful for linguists, humor theorists, and writers assessing whether a joke's funniness culminates properly at the punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal tension principle
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke's text must be constructed so that suspense or unresolved tension peaks at the punchline position; the funniness culminates in the final sentence (the punchline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key requirements: (1) No earlier release of the comic energy — the setup must build rather than discharge. (2) The punchline must be terminal or near-terminal — material after the punchline dilutes it. (3) The punchline carries the maximum surprise — earlier surprises are subordinated to the climax. The defining property is that tension reaches its highest level at the very end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pulse decomposition (single/two/multi-pulse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify punchlines by internal structural complexity: single-pulse (one beat, one twist), two-pulse (a setup within the punchline plus a sub-twist), and multi-pulse (multiple internal beats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-pulse: immediate one-beat effect. Two-pulse: an internal mini-setup then twist within the punchline. Multi-pulse: layered internal architecture often used in longer-form jokes; can extend funniness provided each pulse adds to (rather than dilutes) the climax. Assess how many pulses the punchline contains and whether pulses cumulatively heighten terminal tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sudden recategorization
rubrics_metrics.description: A logical device in which what seemed to belong to category A is revealed to be category B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions by changing the audience's category-assignment for an element of the setup at the terminal moment, producing surprise through reclassification. Evaluate whether the recategorization is clear and placed at terminal position to maximize effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garden-path inversion
rubrics_metrics.description: A logical device where the audience is led down one interpretive path, and the punchline reveals that path was only a setup (i.e., the interpretation is inverted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relies on misdirection: set up a strong but wrong parsing/interpretation and invert it at the punch. Timing and terminal placement are crucial; earlier clues or releases reduce its force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literal-figurative reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: A device where what was taken figuratively is revealed to be literal (or vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates surprise by shifting the intended reading of a phrase or situation. Must be positioned so the reversal occurs at the punchline to produce maximum comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantifier inversion
rubrics_metrics.description: A device in which the expected scope of quantifiers like 'all,' 'none,' or 'some' is inverted at the punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works by exploiting expectation about quantity/scope; the inversion should be the terminal informational update. Assess if the audience's assumed quantifier scope is effectively overturned at the end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference-frame switch
rubrics_metrics.description: A device where identical words or descriptions are revealed to refer to a different referent than the audience assumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates surprise by switching the referential anchor; effectiveness depends on prior assumptions established in the setup and the terminal reveal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicature cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: A device that cancels an implication previously drawn by the audience (what was implied is suddenly negated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relies on conversational implicatures and their cancellation at the punch. The cancellation must occur at terminal position and be detectable as overturning the setup's implicature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A device where the punchline turns back on the structure of the joke itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metalinguistic turn that makes the joke comment on its own format or expectations; must be used so the self-referential twist is the culminating element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position-in-discourse importance (ordering matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke's funniness is partly a function of position-in-discourse: terminal position amplifies funniness while the same line in mid-text loses force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles: (a) A potentially funny line buried mid-text loses much force. (b) Moving the same content to terminal position increases comic effect. (c) Adding text after the punchline can kill the joke entirely. Use these principles when ordering elements of a joke; test reordering to see if the punch must be terminal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-punchline interdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Material after the punchline either functions as a 'tag' (a small pulse capitalizing on the punch) or ruins the joke; explanation, exposition, or aftermath are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed post-punchline material: short tags that add a small pulse and capitalize on the main punch. Disallowed: exposition, explanation, or extended aftermath which dilute or kill the punch. Even a beat of silence is preferable to talking past the punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope exclusions (not applicable genres)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hetzron's terminal-tension analysis excludes continuous-humor texts (parody, satire, comic essays) and slow-build observational comedy where humor is distributed or based on recognition rather than a terminal punch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply terminal-punchline criteria to genres where humor is continuously distributed or where the comic effect accrues gradually; these forms require different evaluative models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic checklist for punchline effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of diagnostic questions to evaluate whether a joke satisfies the terminal-tension and pulse-structure criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions: Where is tension highest in the text? Is it at the end? How many pulses does the punchline contain? What logical device transforms expectation at the punch? Is anything said after the punchline? If so, does it tag or dilute? Could the joke be reordered so the punch is in mid-text? (If yes, it is currently positioned correctly.) Use this checklist to analyze or revise jokes for terminal positioning and pulse architecture.
